SPEC COMPLIANCE CHUNK FP-09: FHIRPath — §5.6.1-§5.6.5 String Manipulation (Search). Test these items: indexOf(substring), substring(start, [length]), startsWith(prefix), endsWith(suffix), contains(substring). For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.evidence: FP-09 HISTORIAN probe showed native C++ returns empty/NULL for resource-backed dynamic arguments such as s.indexOf(term), s.substring(start), s.startsWith(prefix), s.endsWith(suffix), and s.contains(term), while forced Python fallback resolves those arguments in the outer resource focus and returns the expected results. The spec defines functions as operating on an input collection while arguments are FHIRPath expressions; scoped per-item argument focus is only introduced by scoped functions such as where/select.
issues.root_cause: Native Evaluator::evalFunction evaluated FP-09 sourced string-search arguments against the already-evaluated source string collection instead of the outer invocation focus, so sibling resource paths in arguments became empty.
issues.resolution: Evaluate indexOf, substring, startsWith, endsWith, and string-function contains arguments against outer_input for sourced calls, otherwise against the current input. Added native/fallback parity and native sqllogictest coverage, rebuilt and copied the bundled extension.
